_note: Per-cascade-node data transparency entries: exact definition, real series source, and a link an economist can click to verify the number themselves. Consumed by the node drawer in js/cascade.js (openNodeDrawer). Series values are NOT re-fetched here — indicator_id points into the already-loaded data/unified/denmark_wide.json (see js/dashboard.js getTimeSeries). Benchmark-only nodes (no indicator_id) fall back to data/unified/benchmarks.json, fetched lazily on first drawer open.

folkeskole_funding.definition: Real (2024-kr) public grundskole (primary/lower-secondary school) spend per pupil.
folkeskole_funding.source_name: Danmarks Statistik, tables UOE1 + UDDAKT20 + NAHC1 (derived)
folkeskole_funding.caveat: Derived: real 2024-kr public grundskole spend ÷ pupils, PL-deflated using NAHC1. This is the lever, not an outcome — shown here for reference, not simulated.

learning_outcomes.caveat: NOT in Danmarks Statistik — confirmed absent after searching all 2,316 StatBank tables. Core learning-outcome data sits outside the national statistics apparatus; that gap is itself part of the argument.

neet.definition: Share of 16-24-year-olds neither in education nor employment (NEET), Denmark.

income.definition: Average disposable income per person, current kr.

unemployment.definition: Unemployment rate, Labour Force Survey (LFS) definition.
unemployment.caveat: Annual value is the mean of available quarters, not a Q4 snapshot.

life_satisfaction.definition: Grundskole pupil general wellbeing ("generel trivsel"), mean score 1-5, from the national trivselsmåling.
life_satisfaction.caveat: PROXY: measures grundskole-pupil wellbeing specifically, NOT a whole-population Cantril ladder. Units and population differ from the general-population life-satisfaction concept used elsewhere in the dashboard.

life_expectancy.definition: Life expectancy at birth, average of sexes.

hale.definition: Healthy life expectancy (HALE) — years lived in full health.
hale.caveat: No Danish time series exists in this project yet — single-point HLEG benchmark only. This gap is itself part of the argument: core health data alongside GDP is thinner than the money data.

poverty_rate.caveat: No Danish time series exists in this project yet — single-point HLEG benchmark only.
